source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Ask AI (Capella-wide AI chatbot)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - new capellaiq: namespace concept; distinct from capellaiq:capella-iq (the query-editor-scoped assistant covered elsewhere in this batch) since Ask AI is a global, every-page chatbot, not a query-generation tool

relations.subject: capellaiq:ask-ai
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted requiresSetting) - Ask AI is controlled by the same organization-level toggle documented for Capella iQ elsewhere in this batch (see configure-capellaiq.json), confirming the two features share one on/off switch even though Ask AI is presented as a separate product surface
relations.evidence: You can opt out of AI features from the **Settings** tab by unchecking the **Enable Capella iQ** option.

notable_absence.finding: Ask AI has no role, plan, or edition gate stated anywhere on this page - it's described as 'available from every page in Capella' to any user, gated only by a single organization-wide setting (which the page doesn't say who can flip - contrast with configure-capellaiq.md, where flipping the equivalent Capella iQ toggle is explicitly restricted to the Organization Owner role). This is a real access-control asymmetry: the same-named 'Enable Capella iQ' setting is role-gated on one page and not-mentioned-as-role-gated on this one.

cross_component_finding: Ask AI is documented as a public preview feature ('This feature is available as a public preview') using third-party LLMs, and requires accepting Capella's Supplemental Terms before use - the same terms-acceptance mechanism used for Capella iQ (see get-started-with-iq.json, work-with-capellaiq.json). This confirms Ask AI and Capella iQ are governed by the same legal/consent gate even though they are documented as separate features with separate settings labels ('Enable Capella iQ' governs both, per the evidence above).
